sarah: Quick ask — can someone run a combined nsys + torch.profiler capture for the latency regression on the batch=8 benchmark? Suspect KV-cache warmup is different. Need a prod-like run: model=gpt-medium-v2 (pinned), seq=512, kv-cache enabled. Warmup 2 steps, measure 5 steps. Upload scrubbed traces to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2501234567 (tag: kv-warmup-check).
devin: I can take this, which machine should I use? any special launcher flags?
sarah: Prefer RTX-A100 nodes (gpu-3 or gpu-7). Use the continuous batching config we used last week. No sampling/temperature (deterministic). Launcher flags: `--batch-size 8 --seq-len 512 --kv-cache true`. Also capture GPU metrics with nsys.
mike: I can run nsys on gpu-3 now. Will use this capture command (feel free to copy):
```bash
nsys profile --output=/tmp/trace_2501234567 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi --trace=cuda,cudnn,nvtx --sample=none \ 
  --stats=true --env="NSYS_NVTX_ENABLE=1" --force-overwrite -- backfill_run.sh \ 
  --model gpt-medium-v2 --batch 8 --seq 512 --warmup 2 --steps 5
```
mike: For the PyTorch profiler add this snippet right before the measured loop:
```python
with torch.profiler.profile(
    activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.CUDA],
    schedule=torch.profiler.schedule(wait=2, warmup=0, active=5),
    record_shapes=True,
    with_stack=True,
    profile_memory=True,
    on_trace_ready=torch.profiler.tensorboard_trace_handler("/tmp/pt_trace_2501234567")
):
    run_inference_loop()
```
devin: Scrub rules? We should remove any raw prompts and hostnames before upload.
sarah: Yep — redact prompts and PII, strip full env vars and hostnames. Use `tools/scrub_traces.py --strip-args --remove-hosts` before upload. Also compress with `zstd -19` if trace >500MB.
perf-bot: [auto] PERF TASK CREATED: #PERF-987 — requested_by=sarah — tags=[kv-warmup-check] — deadline=2h
mike: Capture started on gpu-3. ETA ~18m. Will run scrub script then upload. @devin @ashok please review after upload.
mike: Uploaded (scrubbed + zstd) to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2501234567/trace_2501234567.nsight.zst and tensorboard run to s3://redwood-perf/traces/2501234567/pt_tb_2501234567.zip
devin: Got it. Downloading now. I'll generate a lightweight flamegraph from the nsys report and drop flamegraph.svg in the same folder.
ashok: Quick things to look for: large `aten::` kernel stalls, excessive `cudaMemcpy` around KV unpack, and any long host-side stalls (scheduling / python GIL). Also check NVTX spans corresponding to cache warmup.
sarah: If the flamegraph shows a split between warmup and steady-state where steady-state has higher kernel latency, that's our regression signal. If it's just warmup overhead, we may need to adjust the warmup policy.
devin: Flamegraph uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/traces/2501234567/flamegraph.svg. Observations: a couple of big hotspots in `transformer_block::forward` and noticeable `cudaLaunchKernel` tail.
ashok: I'll jump on the flamegraph now. If we need further traces, let's capture a smaller microbenchmark that isolates KV cache misses (single-layer short-run). @mike if you can spare another 2-3 captures later that'd help.
mike: Yep I can run the microbench after this. Tagging notes into #PERF-987.
sarah: Thanks all. If we don't converge by EOD let's do a short sync at 15:00 PT. Otherwise keep comments on the S3 folder. :thumbsup:
